objective: Prove that for a fair contact with a visible bit and three hidden places the twist (flipping literal polarities across a seam) depends only on its cohomology class exactly when the contact's two relations are exchanged by flipping all three places; that independent fair polarities make every twist invisible; that a visible bit with two hidden places gives a two-literal world; that the monotone contact contradicts in a twist only if the dual cubic graph has no 2-factor in the twist's dual class; and that when the patterns allowed by both relations tile the plane, the twists in which the tiling closes never contradict and in the others every minimal contradiction winds.
status: Proved by TRIPLE-TWIST-20261023-001A-P001 (V1 prose proof; own-solver checks on random tori, all 65,536 contact pairs, all small triangular tori and all 54 tiling placements; two controls rejected). For fair three-place contacts a twist depends only on its class exactly when the contact is complement-closed; otherwise a contractible seam is a defect. Independent fair polarities hide every twist; two hidden places give two-literal worlds. The monotone contact contradicts only without a dual 2-factor in the twist's class and never contradicts on triangular tori with sides 2 to 5. For complement-closed contacts whose doubly allowed patterns tile the plane, planar patches and fitting twists never contradict, and every minimal contradiction winds along a lattice on which the twist differs from every fitting twist, so lines run along classes the relative twist makes odd. A first statement of Proposition 4 was false on four two-row tori and is corrected.
title: Proof: when a three-place twist is defined, hidden, frozen or forced to wind
